app.name: InsightQuest
chat.title: Ask the data
chat.placeholder: Ask about installations, purchases or delays
chat.intro: Ask in plain language. Answers are calculated on this server; nothing is sent anywhere.
chat.how_caption: A fixed, validated analysis run on this server. Counts are source rows, not distinct devices.
chat.local: Calculated on this server. Nothing was sent to OpenAI.
chat.rows_note: Based on {rows} source rows; {excluded} left out (missing or invalid dates).
chat.h.type_high: {n} {noun} for {label}, the highest of {k} device types
chat.h.type_low: {n} {noun} for {label}, the lowest of {k} device types
chat.h.delay_type_high: {n} days (median) for {label}, the slowest of {k} device types
chat.h.delay_type_low: {n} days (median) for {label}, the fastest of {k} device types
chat.h.delay_period: Median delay between {lo} and {hi} days across {k} periods
chat.empty: Nothing matches this scope. Try a wider date range.
chat.unsupported: I can't answer that yet. The closest question I can answer:
chat.ambiguous: That mixes two things. Pick one:
chat.unclear: I didn't quite get that. Try one of these:
chat.error: Sorry, I couldn't calculate that. Please check the data source settings and try again.
chat.ai.toggle: Let the AI explain results (sends aggregated numbers to OpenAI)
chat.ai.payload: What would be sent to OpenAI
chat.ai.payload_caption: Only these aggregated numbers are sent when you press Explain. No question, history, records, IDs, coordinates or device type names.
chat.ai.blocked: AI explanation is unavailable because a group has fewer than {min} rows.
chat.ai.label: AI explanation (generated text; check it against the numbers above)
chat.ai.interpret: Let the AI interpret my question (sends the question text to OpenAI)
chat.ai.proposal: The AI read your question as: {what}
chat.ai.unsupported: The AI could not map that question to a supported analysis.

state.columns_missing: Required columns are missing from the data source: {columns}.
state.no_rows: No rows found in the selected date range.
state.row_limit_reached: Row limit reached ({limit} rows). Narrow the date range or raise the maximum rows to see everything.
state.proxy_date_warning: PurchaseDate is a warranty-start proxy, not a confirmed shipping date
page.overview_desc: Map, territory trends, projections and data diagnostics for monitor installations.
ask.description: The model plans; your server validates and calculates.
common.period_help: Group results by day, week or month (weeks start on Monday).
col.label: Label
sidebar.from_date_help: First day included. Shared by every analysis page.
sidebar.to_date_help: Last day included. Shared by every analysis page.
sidebar.max_rows_help: Upper limit on rows read for this analysis. Raise it for complete results, lower it for speed.
sidebar.refresh_help: Clear cached query results and read the data source again.
state.date_order_error: From date must be earlier than or equal to To date.
state.demo_banner: DEMO MODE — synthetic data from {file}; no database data is used.
state.config_invalid: The configuration is invalid: {detail}. Fix the setting in your .env file or environment and restart the app.

state.read_only_warning: The database login can write to the source table. Use a read-only account for this dashboard.
home.tagline: Answers to six business questions about monitor purchases, installations and stock.
home.guide_caption: Each card shows whether your column mappings support the question: Ready, Partial (some fields missing) or Not available.
home.kpi_devices_help: All devices in the source, regardless of the date range.
home.kpi_unavailable: Headline figures need the installation date and a product type or territory mapping.
q1.top_n_help: How many of the highest and lowest periods to rank for each series.
q1.definition: Purchases are devices whose purchase date falls in the period; installations are devices whose install date falls in the period. Both are device counts (one row per device).
q1.flat_series: Series {measure}: the values are flat, so there are no peaks or lows.
q1.axis_gap: Purchased but not yet installed (cumulative devices)
q1.summary: {measure}: peak of {peak} devices in the period starting {peak_date}; lowest {low} in the period starting {low_date}; average {mean} per period.
q1.gap_summary: Net change over the range: {gap} devices (purchases minus installations). A rising line means a growing backlog of devices waiting to be installed.
q2.definition: Installed rate = devices with an install date ÷ all devices in the group. Gap = the group's rate minus the overall rate, in percentage points. Customer size is the number of devices a company owns (see the legend).
q2.metric_devices_help: All devices in this breakdown (not limited by the date range).
q2.rate_definition: Devices with an install date ÷ all devices.
q2.summary: Lowest installed rate: {worst} at {worst_rate}% ({worst_gap} points versus the overall {overall}%). Highest: {best} at {best_rate}%.
q2.small_group_note: Groups with fewer than {threshold} devices are flagged as small. Their rates swing easily, so interpret them with care.
q3.definition: Lag = install date minus shipment date, in whole days, for devices shipped within the selected range and installed by the To date. Only devices with both dates are measured; installs recorded before shipment are excluded and counted separately.
q3.no_valid_lags: No device has a valid shipment-to-installation lag in this range ({negative} were installed before their shipment date).
q3.matched_help: Devices with both dates and a non-negative lag. This is the denominator of every figure on this page.
q3.negative_help: Excluded from the statistics: the install date is earlier than the shipment date.
q3.summary: Half of the devices were installed within {median} days of shipment and 90% within {p90} days. The most common range is {top_bin} ({top_share} of devices).
q3.censoring_note: Only devices that already have an install date are measured, so recent shipments look faster than they will end up (slow installs are not observed yet).
q3.cohort_summary: Median lag: {first} days for {first_month} shipments, {last} days for {last_month} shipments. Recent months look faster partly because slow installs are not observed yet.
q3.cohort_note: Each point is the month a group of devices was shipped. Months with few devices swing easily.
state.demo_mapping_hint: Demo mode is on, but these column settings point to columns that are not in the demo file: {variables}. They probably come from your .env or environment. Blank them (set them to empty) or remove them to use the demo defaults.
q4.horizon_help: How many months ahead to forecast.
q4.definition: Rates use {rows} devices purchased in the selected range (one row per device). The latest complete month is shown in the cards; open 'How the rates are calculated' for every denominator.
q4.summary: {month}: {cohort}% of the devices purchased that month were installed by month-end; {mature}% have been installed to date.
q4.negative_note: {count} devices have an install date before their purchase date. They are not counted as installed but stay in the denominator.
q4.maturity_note: Recent months are still maturing: devices purchased lately have had little time to be installed, so their rates keep rising as time passes.
q4.partial_note: The month starting {month} is incomplete and is left out of the chart and cards.
q4.forecast_unavailable: Not enough history for a forecast: {message}
q4.forecast_summary: Dashed line with diamonds: forecast for the next {horizon} months. The shaded band is ± the average backtest error of {mae} installs (model: {model}; {folds} backtest months).
q5.include_last_help: The latest month may be incomplete. Leave unchecked to exclude it from trends and forecasts.
q5.definition: Markets are your own territories and product types, assessed from purchase history. Predictability is how closely a rolling one-step-ahead forecast matched what happened in past months (100 = perfect). No external market data is used.
q5.overall_title: Overall purchases: trend, forecast and predictability
q5.score_help: 100 × (1 − WAPE) from a rolling one-step-ahead backtest. High ≥ 75, Medium ≥ 50, otherwise Low.
q5.label: Predictability
q5.wape_help: Sum of absolute forecast errors ÷ sum of actual purchases over the backtest months.
q5.insufficient_overall: Not enough history for a reliable backtest. {message}
q5.overall_summary: Predictability is {label} (score {score}/100). Over the last {folds} months the one-step forecast missed by {wape}% overall (average error {mae} devices; model: {model}). The shaded band around the dashed forecast for the next {horizon} months is ± that average error.
q5.history_summary: {months} months of history. The forecast appears once there is enough history.
q5.insufficient_markets: Insufficient history (fewer than {months} months) for: {markets}. They are listed in the table without a score.
q5.comparison_unavailable: Growth and share change need at least {months} months of history, so they are not shown.
q6.as_of_help: Demand is measured over the window ending on this date. Defaults to today (live data) or the latest date in the demo data.
q6.caveat: On hand = devices that have no install date. This overstates warehouse stock, so treat the results as a simulation, not a stock count. Lead time, safety days, maximum cover and the demand window are adjustable assumptions.
q6.on_hand_note: Devices with no install date (overstates warehouse stock)
q6.chart_legend: Bars: devices on hand. Triangles ▲: reorder point (demand × lead time). Squares ■: maximum stock (demand × maximum cover).
q6.summary_ok: No product type is at stockout or reorder risk, based on demand over the last {window} days.
q6.summary_risk: At or near stockout: {names}. The earliest projected stockout is {date} (demand over the last {window} days).
q6.rule.stockout_risk: On hand is below demand × lead time.
q6.rule.reorder: On hand is at or below demand × (lead time + safety days).
q6.rule.healthy: None of the other conditions apply.
q6.rule.overstock: On hand is above demand × maximum cover days.
q6.rule.no_demand: No installs in the demand window, so cover cannot be computed.
inventory.lead_time_days_help: Days between ordering and receiving stock.
inventory.safety_days_help: Extra days of demand kept as a buffer above the reorder point.
inventory.max_cover_days_help: Stock above demand × this many days counts as overstock.
inventory.demand_window_days_help: Number of recent days used to measure demand (installs per day).
overview.projection_help: How many periods ahead to project.
overview.map_empty: No mappable rows found for the selected period. If your device location is not 'lat,lon', configure IQ_COL_LATITUDE and IQ_COL_LONGITUDE.
overview.map_no_clusters: No cluster points are available from the current map data.
overview.map_summary: {rows} installed devices with coordinates, grouped into {clusters} clusters. Bigger circles mean more installs.
overview.pick_territory: Select at least one territory to display installs.
overview.territory_summary: {top} has the most installs in the range ({count}). Each install is attributed to the territory of the device's current owner company.
overview.customers_help: Select one or more customers for the trend and projection. The five busiest are preselected.
overview.pick_customer: Select at least one customer to display the trend and projection.
overview.not_enough_data: Not enough data to build a trend.
overview.projection_summary: Solid line: installs to date. Dashed line with diamonds: projection for the next {periods} periods ({period}).
overview.backtest_none: Not enough history for backtesting. Use a longer date range to compute MAE, RMSE and MAPE.
overview.diagnostics_summary: {total} devices were installed in the range. Coordinates and customers are needed for the map and the customer trend.
home.howto_1: **Pick a question.** Each card gives the answer at a glance; open it for charts and tables.
home.howto_2: **Filters are shared.** The date range in the sidebar applies to every page.
home.howto_3: **Ask the chat.** Use the chat button in the corner for questions in your own words.
home.answer.q1_installs: Installs peaked in {peak_month} ({peak}) and were lowest in {low_month} ({low}).
home.answer.q1_purchases: Purchases peaked in {peak_month} ({peak}) and were lowest in {low_month} ({low}).
home.answer.q2: Lowest installed share by {dimension}: {group} at {rate}%, versus {overall}% overall.
home.answer.q3: Typically {median} days from shipment to installation; 9 in 10 are done within {p90} days.
home.answer.q4: {rate}% of devices bought in {month} were installed that month; {mature}% by now.
home.answer.q5: {market} is the most predictable market ({label} predictability){trend}.
home.answer.q6: {risk} of {total} device types are at stockout risk or due to reorder; {excess} overstocked.
home.reason.no_rows: no data in the selected date range
home.reason.flat: activity is flat over the selected range
home.reason.no_segment: no territory or product type column is mapped
home.reason.error: the figure could not be computed (details were logged)
